title: Business owner between signing and closing on a company sale: net proceeds, escrows and the tax reserve
notes: Dermot gives the net closing wire as 11.1 million and about twelve minutes later Renata reads the draft funds flow memo showing 10,496,300 (the first figure was before banker and legal fees), which also moves the amount phased into the moderate model from eight and a half to 7.9 million; the transcript first renders the closing date as October 13th and the buyer as Chorister, both clarified only after the associate joins, and the next meeting is first floated for the 13th before landing on Wednesday, October 14. The wire-instruction letter moves from Lowell to Dermot because deal counsel accepts only seller-signed instructions with a callback, the IPS due date moves from Friday to September 29, the closing recap omits the COBRA comparison, Renata's document forwarding and the clients' own DocuSign signing (i7, which shares every noun with the associate's i1 and differs only in who acts); the loss of the Tallowbrook group health plan at closing is keyed as part of e2 (Dermot stops being an employee), so a separately listed health-coverage event matches neither e1 nor e2 and goes to adjudication, as does a client item to read and sign the revised IPS. The mortgage payoff and the $200,000 stake in Wes Hollingshed's shop are explicitly deferred and the $400,000 donor-advised fund proposal is declined, so none of them is an action.

primary_goal.expected: Preserve the proceeds from the sale of the business and turn them into income that lasts the rest of both their lives

retirement_target.expected: Dermot fully retires at the end of his 12-month consulting agreement with the buyer, end of October 2027, at age 62 (the 2024 plan assumed 65); Renata is already retired
